cars.generation: Original TE27 Levin/Trueno road family on second-generation E20 Corolla platform
cars.variant: Corolla Levin 2T-G — 1972 Japan road reference in manufacturer history
cars.specification_market: Original TE27 first Levin / Trueno production-road family on the second-generation E20 Corolla/Sprinter coupe platform. Selected 1972 Japan 2T-G Levin road reference is Toyota UK’s manufacturer historical account: 1588 cc, 115 PS at 6400 rpm, 105 lb-ft at 5200 rpm, 855 kg kerb mass and Solex carburetion. Output is quoted as stated; that page does not establish a gross/net test basis, so none is asserted and no SAE/net conversion is inferred. Group sister Trueno, years, grades and facelift within one TE27 programme; do not add the sister badge separately. Existing AE86 cars are a later generation, not this entry. No ordinary TE25/OHV engine, US SR5, race tune, 151E sixteen-valve head, near-200-hp competition output, dimensions, transmission, tyres, brakes, compression ratio or actual measured performance imported. Production engine’s eight valves are separately supported by Toyota’s motorsport history.
cars.summary: The original TE27 Corolla Levin / Sprinter Trueno put the Celica’s 2T-G twin-cam engine into a lighter road coupe in 1972 and established the sporting lineage later associated with the AE86. Toyota documents its place in the early Corolla WRC programme. This road-car foundation earns admission; the later 151E sixteen-valve rally engine and its results are kept separate from stock specifications.

sources.title: Toyota Corolla generations: 1970–74 — Joe Clifford, 1 July 2013; updated 26 July 2024
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer model-history and road-specification account
sources.notes: Full relevant article body read, including Levin introduction, powertrain and chassis context. Selected TE27 2T-G road figures only. Output basis remains unspecified on this page, not relabelled as modern net/SAE. General Corolla equipment lists do not prove exact Levin equipment. Article compresses the 1975 rally story; the more specific Toyota global motorsport account controls separation of production eight-valve 2T-G and later sixteen-valve 151E competition engines.

sources.title: Corolla and Motor Sports — 14 November 2016, early TE27 programme
sources.notes: Complete relevant early-Corolla section read. Explicitly links 1972 lighter 20-series Levin/Trueno production road cars with the 2T-G and TE27 identity; says early Group 2 programme used the production eight-valve engine. Separately identifies the TE25/2T-B at the 1973 Press-on-Regardless win and the later 151E sixteen-valve rally engine at the 1975 1000 Lakes victory. Neither race-car output nor race-car specifications are copied to this road record. Later Corolla WRC and AE86 discussion do not supply TE27 attributes.
